title: Affine complexes have sheaf Tor amplitude exactly when their module complexes do
statement: Let A be a ring and X = Spec(A) [def-pc-scheme]. Let M^\bullet be a complex of A-modules and let E be the corresponding object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\subseteq D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] under the affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. For integers a\le b, the following are equivalent: (i) E has Tor amplitude in [a,b], meaning that H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)=0 for every \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal G and every i\notin[a,b]; (ii) M^\bullet has Tor amplitude in [a,b], meaning that H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)=0 for every A-module N and every i\notin[a,b].

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.10.4 (Tag 08E9; label lemma-tor-amplitude-affine), part (1)

proof.text: Assume M^\bullet has Tor amplitude in [a,b]. By [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model], choose a complex P^\bullet of flat A-modules concentrated in [a,b] and an isomorphism M^\bullet\cong P^\bullet in D(A). Under [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], E is isomorphic to the associated complex \widetilde{P^\bullet}. The associated complex is K-flat by [lem-pc-affine-tilde-kflat]. By the convention for the derived tensor product fixed in [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde] (the total tensor complex of a K-flat resolution of the first factor with the second), for every \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal G the derived tensor E\otimes^\mathbf L\mathcal G is represented by the ordinary tensor complex \widetilde{P^\bullet}\otimes\mathcal G. Since P^\bullet is zero outside [a,b], so is this tensor complex, and its cohomology vanishes there; hence E has Tor amplitude in [a,b].

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.10.4 (Tag 08E9), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: Assume E has Tor amplitude in [a,b] and let N be an A-module. By [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], E\cong\widetilde{M^\bullet}, so [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde, part (3)] (with N^\bullet=N in degree 0) gives E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}\widetilde N\cong\widetilde{K^\bullet} in D(\mathcal O_X), where K^\bullet is a complex of A-modules representing M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N. The functor Q\mapsto\widetilde Q is exact, since on stalks it is localization [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] and localization is exact; hence H^i(\widetilde{K^\bullet})\cong\widetilde{H^i(K^\bullet)}. An A-module Q with \widetilde Q=0 is zero, because Q\cong\Gamma(X,\widetilde Q) [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction, part (2)]. Taking \mathcal G=\widetilde N in (i), for i\notin[a,b] we get \widetilde{H^i(K^\bullet)}=0, so H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)=0. Thus M^\bullet has Tor amplitude in [a,b].

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.10.4 (Tag 08E9), proof, second paragraph
